report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Public append/read/verify API for the council transcript chain.

symbols.name: append_round
symbols.note: Normalizes, secret-floors, sorts, and chains a round of turns; returns chained IDs. Raises ValueError on empty turns or duplicate actors.

symbols.name: append_turn
symbols.note: Convenience wrapper for append_round with a single turn; returns the first chained ID.

symbols.name: append_roster
symbols.note: Chains a roster accounting record with derived counts and a degraded flag; raises ValueError on invalid phase, actor, or outcome.

symbols.name: load_transcript
symbols.note: Reads all JSON lines, skipping blank and unparseable lines; missing file yields [].

symbols.name: transcript_head
symbols.note: Returns (record_count, last entry_sha) by loading the transcript; None head if empty.

symbols.name: read_anchor
symbols.note: Reads the anchor file as JSON; returns None if missing or unparseable.

symbols.name: verify_chain
symbols.note: Walks the chain, checking body_sha, entry_sha, and prev linkage; optionally checks count/head against anchor or explicit expectations.

claims.text: Turns may arrive in ANY completion order.
claims.why: The function sorts by (actor, role, status, canonical_body_json) before chaining, so completion order is irrelevant to the chain.

claims.text: Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with seq assigned here -- so reversed completion order yields a byte-identical chain head.
claims.why: The sort key includes actor first and the chain is built from the sorted list; reversed input order produces the same sequence. Secret-flooring is done in _normalize_turn (defined elsewhere), but the claim about ordering is satisfied.

claims.text: Returns the ids in CHAINED order.
claims.why: The function returns the result of _chain_records, which returns ids in chain order per the code at the top of this chunk.

claims.text: Exactly one turn per actor per round is allowed: a duplicate is a caller bug that would double a voice...
claims.why: The code counts actors and raises ValueError if any actor (excluding 'council.redacted.redacted') appears more than once.

claims.text: ...a missing participant must be recorded as an unavailable turn rather than skipped.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the code that enforces or documents the unavailable-turn requirement; it is a policy statement without a visible check here.

claims.text: The offending bytes never reach the file -- not in the turn, and not in the receipt.
claims.why: The refusal receipt is constructed and substituted, but the actual file write happens in _chain_records (defined elsewhere); this chunk cannot confirm the bytes never reach the file.

claims.text: Canonical body is the final tiebreak so the order is TOTAL even when two anonymised refusal receipts collapse to the same actor: chaining must not inherit wall-clock completion order from anywhere.
claims.why: The sort key includes canonical_body_json(r) as the last component, making the order total and deterministic.

claims.text: Convenience over append_round; prefer the round form so ordering stays deterministic.
claims.why: append_turn simply delegates to append_round with a single-turn list, so the ordering properties are inherited.

claims.text: Chain the roster accounting: requested / seated / responded / unavailable with machine reasons, plus the DISTINCT INDEPENDENCE CLASS count and a degraded flag whenever fewer participants responded than were requested.
claims.why: The record includes requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes over heard_classes, and degraded = responded < requested.

claims.text: Counts are DERIVED here, never accepted from the caller: '3 of 4' and '2 of 2' must not be able to render as the same string...
claims.why: All counts (requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes) are computed from the normalized participants, not taken from caller-supplied fields.

claims.text: ...a consumer that shows the participant count instead of the distinct-class count is showing a council of clones as a council.
claims.why: This is a policy statement about consumers; the chunk only defines the record fields, not how consumers display them.

claims.text: Read all records, skipping a torn tail line (never fatal). Missing is [].
claims.why: The function returns [] when the file does not exist, and skips lines that fail json.loads (including a torn tail).

claims.text: (record_count, head_entry_sha) -- the tail anchor, recomputed from the file. Compare against read_anchor to catch a truncation.
claims.why: The function returns (len(records), records[-1].get('entry_sha')) from load_transcript, which reads the file.

claims.text: Three independent checks per line: body_sha recomputed over the canonical body -- catches a content edit; entry_sha recomputed over (prev, stored body_sha, ts) -- catches a back-dated ts or a rewritten link where body_sha WAS updated; prev equals the previous line's entry_sha -- catches a deleted or reordered line...
claims.why: The loop compares _body_sha(rec) to stored_body, _entry_sha(rec.get('prev'), stored_body, rec.get('ts')) to stored_entry, and rec.get('prev') to prev_entry_sha.

claims.text: TAIL truncation is the one deletion a per-line walk cannot catch... so the persisted anchor is consulted by default and a shortfall in count or head is NAMED. Explicit expected_count / expected_head override it; use_anchor=False verifies linkage only.
claims.why: The function reads the anchor when use_anchor and no explicit expectations, then appends failures for count/head mismatches; use_anchor=False skips the anchor read.

claims.text: Never a bare False.
claims.why: The function always returns (ok, failures) where failures is a list, never returns a bare boolean.

claims.text: Every failure NAMES the 1-indexed line and what mismatched.
claims.why: All failure strings include 'line {i}' or, for whole-file issues, describe the missing/truncated state with expected counts/heads.

claims.text: A check that CANNOT FAIL: an assertion comparing something with itself, a test whose fixture is derived from the thing under test, a branch no input reaches.
claims.why: No such self-referential check exists in this chunk; all comparisons are against independently stored values.

claims.text: A refusal with NO REACHABLE REPAIR: code that reports an error and names a fix another rule in this same file forbids.
claims.why: No such refusal exists; the only refusals are ValueError raises for bad input, and the refusal-receipt path substitutes a receipt rather than naming a forbidden fix.

claims.text: A rule INVERTED with respect to its own stated goal: it blocks the narrow precise action and permits the broad one.
claims.why: No inverted rule is present; the restrictions (phase, actor regex, outcome set) are narrow and the allowed paths are the intended ones.

claims.text: A value parsed from output whose FORMAT IS NOT PINNED: a parser that will silently report 'absent' rather than 'unreadable' when its input changes shape.
claims.why: read_anchor returns None on JSONDecodeError, which could be considered 'absent' rather than 'unreadable', but the docstring does not promise to distinguish; load_transcript skips unparseable lines by design. No format is pinned here, so the claim is not violated.

observations.what: append_roster counts 'refused' as seated but not as responded; the 'degraded' flag is based on responded < requested, so a refused participant counts toward seated but not toward responded, which may understate degradation.

append_round excludes 'council.redacted.redacted' from duplicate detection but that actor could still appear in the chain; the comment says 'a duplicate is a caller bug', but this exclusion may allow intentional duplicates for redacted refusals.
verify_chain skips blank lines without incrementing n_records; a blank line between records does not break linkage but also does not affect the count, which could mask a tampered blank line.
read_anchor returns None on JSONDecodeError, conflating 'no anchor' with 'corrupt anchor'; verify_chain would then treat the anchor as absent and skip the truncation check.

load_transcript uses errors='replace' when reading, which can silently corrupt non-UTF8 bytes into replacement characters; a tampered file with invalid UTF-8 would be read as valid JSON lines with mangled content, potentially bypassing verification.

risks: append_roster | low | Refused participants count as seated but not responded, so degraded may be true when all participants responded as refused; check whether refusal should count as a response for the degraded flag.

append_round | low | The duplicate-actor exclusion for 'council.redacted.redacted' could allow two redacted turns from the same actor, undermining the one-turn-per-actor rule; verify the refusal-receipt path prevents this.
verify_chain | low | Blank lines are skipped without affecting n_records; a tampered blank line inserted between records would not be flagged, though it does not break linkage.

read_anchor | medium | JSONDecodeError in read_anchor returns None, so a corrupt anchor file is treated as absent and truncation checks are silently skipped; consider distinguishing 'missing' from 'unreadable'.

load_transcript | medium | errors='replace' can silently replace invalid UTF-8 bytes, potentially allowing a tampered file to be read as valid JSON; consider using strict decoding or reporting corruption.
